subject: [PATCH RFC] mm/zswap: reference the pool by index to shrink struct zswap_entry

reviews.author: Yosry Ahmed
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Yosry Ahmed noted that the number of pools is bounded by the number of compression algorithms, and suggested using a fixed array of 256 elements indexed by a u8 to avoid wasting memory; they also questioned the need for an xarray and proposed removing it or reusing the linked list

Reviewer noted that the current design uses an xarray for zswap pools, which is unnecessary given that there are only a limited number of compression algorithms and most systems use one; they suggested replacing it with a fixed array to reduce memory usage and complexity.
reviews.raw_body:
Hmm yeah good point, we do reuse the pools for the same compressors. I
don't know if crypto defines an upper limit on the number of
compression algorithms. If we want to be really conservative we can
use an array of 256 elements indexed by a u8. That's 1KB of memory,
probably mostly wasted. We can also just define an artificial limit on
the number of compressors based on what we currently have implemented
and increase it when needed?

Not sure what's an easy way to determine all crypto compression
algorithms we have tho.

---

Also a good point, I think we may be able to drop the list, and I
think that's ultimately more valuable than the memory savings. It's
unneeded complexity.

reviews.author: Nhat Pham (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged that the number of pools created is limited by the compression algorithm set at runtime, and agreed that a fixed array of 16 elements would be sufficient.
reviews.raw_body:
Seems like we only create new pool when we set a new compression algo right?

In a sense, it's not really about how many compression algorithm we
compile or support at runtime. It's the compression algo that we
actually set (zswap_setup() and zswap_compressor_param_set()). And
it's usually 1 (or 2 if we misconfigure the build config, lol).

I think 16 is already plenty for this purpose, but who knows :)

reviews.author: Yosry Ahmed
reviews.summary: reviewer noted that the patch breaks support for switching compressors at runtime, which is currently possible in the kernel, and requested a justification for breaking this feature
reviews.raw_body:
Technically, you can switch compressors at runtime. Not sure if anyone
actually does this, but it is supported today, and ideally we wouldn't
break it without good reason.

2026-07-27.patch_summary: This patch modifies the zswap compression algorithm to reference its pool by index instead of dynamically creating a new one for each algorithm, which is usually only one or two algorithms are actually used.

reviews.author: Jianyue Wu
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Jianyue Wu noted that the current implementation creates a new pool only when setting a new compression algorithm, which is usually just one or two algorithms in practice, and suggested that 16 pre-allocated pools are already sufficient for this purpose.

The reviewer ran e2e benchmark tests comparing baseline and the RFC patch, but did not observe a measurable performance regression, instead noting that certain compression algorithms (zswap crypto-sg zstd and lzo) are slower than others.

Reviewer Jianyue Wu prefers to drop the xarray and use a fixed-size array of 16 entries, each indexed by a u8, allowing for runtime compressor switching while keeping the ability to increase the number of supported compressors as needed.

Reviewer Jianyue Wu agreed that the dynamic list of compression algorithms is unnecessary complexity and offered to try dropping it; they also suggested considering dropping the obj_cgroup pointer on non-MEMCG systems, but deemed it not worth pursuing
reviews.raw_body:
On Tue, Jul 28, 2026 at 1:07 AM Yosry Ahmed <yosry@kernel.org> wrote:

Thanks Yosry and Nhat for the review.

---

I ran zswap e2e benchmark comparing baseline vs this RFC and did not
observe a measurable performance regression.
BTW, it seems zswap crypto-sg zstd and lzo are slower than zcomp.
Throughput in MB/s:
 alg      | acomp store | zcomp store | acomp load | zcomp load
----------+-------------+-------------+------------+-----------
 lzo      |        1140 |        1710 |       1070 |       1070
 lzo-rle  |        1490 |        1320 |       2030 |       2070
 lz4      |        1520 |        1600 |       1710 |       1870
 lz4hc    |         640 |         680 |       1770 |       1850
 zstd     |         740 |        1190 |        980 |       1720
 deflate  |         180 |         180 |        665 |        660
But that's another topic.

---

I prefer dropping the xarray and go with 16 entries indexed by a u8,
keeping runtime compressor switching, which can increase when needed.

---

Agreed, the list looks like unneeded complexity, will have a try to drop it.
Looks obj_cgroup pointer can also be dropped on !MEMCG, but zswap usually use
in server with cgroup, maybe not worth pursuing.

Best regards,
Jianyue

2026-07-28.patch_summary: This patch modifies the zswap compression algorithm to reference its pool by index instead of dynamically creating a new one for each algorithm, which is usually only one or two algorithms are actually used.
